slug: 2024-01-01 CRVS Systems - DR Congo civil registration snapshot

facts.fact: The Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems snapshot, from a questionnaire completed by the Civil Registration Division in March 2019, states that computers are not used in the civil registration process, that all registrations are paper-based, and that mobile technology is not used in any part of it; each act is written with four carbon copies.
facts.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)

facts.fact: The snapshot (Civil Registration Division questionnaire, March 2019) states that all registrations of births, deaths, marriages and divorces are paper-based, so no event is registered digitally.
facts.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)

facts.fact: The snapshot (Civil Registration Division questionnaire, March 2019) counts 979 local civil registration offices at chiefdom/sector level, 102 urban and 877 rural, each with a civil registrar, and states that none uses a computer or mobile device in registration: 0 of 979.
facts.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)

facts.fact: The snapshot names the Ministry of Interior and Security as the ministry responsible for civil registration and its Civil Registration Division (Bureau de l'État Civil) as the agency, in a centralised system (questionnaire of March 2019).
facts.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)

facts.fact: The snapshot states that a Strategic Plan for 2013-2018 was drafted without using the 2012 evaluation, and that a comprehensive assessment and a costed national CRVS strategy and implementation plan were still to be produced with World Bank/Global Financing Facility support (questionnaire of March 2019); no plan in force is named.
facts.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)

facts.fact: The snapshot gives US$20 million from the World Bank and Global Financing Facility for 2016-2020 as the budgetary supplement from partners and records the government treasury allocation for fiscal year July 2018-June 2019 as 'not available'; the Civil Registration Division names UNICEF and GFF as its main financial partners (questionnaire of March 2019).
facts.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)

systems.system: civil registration system (Bureau de l'État Civil)
systems.platform: none: paper registers with four carbon copies
systems.owner: Ministry of Interior and Security, Civil Registration Division
systems.tiers: 979 local civil registration offices at chiefdom/sector level (102 urban, 877 rural); copies archived at the local office, the High Court registry and the Central Records Office in Kinshasa; secondary offices in reference hospitals planned

systems.owner: listed as support from the Italian Development Cooperation and the World Bank/Global Financing Facility
systems.tiers: not stated; listed as a kind of support, with no progress reported

systems.system: health facility notification of births and deaths
systems.tiers: not stated; health facilities act as notifiers, the link with civil registration offices being 'weak'; no digital means described

systems.owner: listed as support from the Italian Development Cooperation and the World Bank/Global Financing Facility

systems.tiers: none: the snapshot states DR Congo does not have one in place (2019); ONIP is named only as a member of the CRVS Steering Committee

The readlist's published date of 2024-01-01 is a proxy: the PDF is copyright 2019 and rests on a questionnaire of March 2019, so every fact is dated 2019-03.
